headline_marked: Discord [[public server messages]] to appear in Google search results
headline: Discord public server messages to appear in Google search results
summary: Starting mid-December, public Discord messages will be indexed by search engines. Users and admins can opt out.
details: Discord is implementing a significant change to its Discoverable Servers, which are large communities with over 1,000 members that don't require an invitation to join. Starting November 16, these servers will feature Server Web Pages that display basic information and summaries of discussions. This move aims to make information from these communities more accessible via web searches, similar to how Reddit threads appear.

By mid-December, individual messages posted in public channels of these Discoverable Servers will also be indexed and appear word-for-word in search engine results and on Server Web Pages. Importantly, neither the channel summaries nor the individual messages will display the poster's username or avatar, offering a degree of anonymity.

This policy change is limited to Discoverable Servers, with private servers, DMs, and Group DMs remaining entirely private. However, the decision comes at a time when Discord is already facing scrutiny over its privacy policies, potentially sparking new debates about user data.

Server administrators for Discoverable Servers can proactively opt out specific channels from being included in the web presence. Furthermore, individual users have the ability to prevent their posts in Discoverable Servers from being indexed by adjusting settings in the Data and Privacy section of their Discord User Settings.

In regions like the EU, UK, Canada, Brazil, Australia, and South Korea, channel messages will be opt-out by default to comply with local regulations. Users in these areas must manually opt in if they wish for their messages to be searchable. Teen users are also excluded from opting in until they reach adulthood.

topic: anthropic claude ai expands to us government
headline_marked: [[Claude AI]] discount for US government saves $1 billion
headline: Claude AI discount for US government saves $1 billion
summary: The AI model's enterprise and API offerings will see a 40% price reduction for federal, state, and local agencies.
details: Anthropic is expanding its partnership with the General Services Administration (GSA) to offer significant discounts on its AI models. Government agencies can now get Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government, and the Claude API at a 40% reduced price.

This new agreement extends the discount to all product surfaces, including direct purchases and future cloud provider integrations. The savings are also available to state, local, tribal, and territorial governments, potentially saving the government an estimated $1 billion.

The program aims to make advanced AI tools more accessible for public sector use, enabling agencies to tackle complex challenges like managing backlogs, modernizing code, and processing records without substantial upfront costs.

Claude for Government, which offers near-feature parity with commercial offerings at a FedRAMP High authorization level, is already used by approximately 500 US government organizations. Weekly active users have surged eightfold since February, with federal civilian agency usage growing 20-fold in the past year.

Agencies can utilize Claude for sensitive unclassified work. The AI model is also available through Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud's Vertex AI, with specific models authorized for DoD IL4 and IL5 workloads in AWS GovCloud.
Anthropic is also launching a dedicated program to help agencies implement and maximize their use of Claude, bringing private sector best practices to public sector partners.
